small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose kernel dominates runtime (fast_p≈0.64). Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OC (e.g. 256) and BLOCK_IC=64 to better feed `tl.dot`, and try `num_stages=4` on the larger tiles for better K-loop pipelining.
- Move the `for ic_start` loop to be the outermost loop inside the kh/kw nest collapsed into a single (kh*KW+kw) flat loop, so the inner `tl.dot` accumulates across IC without recomputing `ih/iw` masks per ic-tile; or hoist `valid`/`x_sp_off` once and stream BLOCK_IC across all (kh,kw) for better register reuse.
- Since IC=64 and KH=KW=3, set BLOCK_IC=64 (single ic iteration) and unroll the 9 (kh,kw) iterations to eliminate inner-loop overhead.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a scatter-add ConvTranspose: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), compute `input × weight` outer product (GEMM with BLOCK_IC × BLOCK_OC) and scatter-add into the output grid with atomics — avoids the gather-side modulo/stride checks that currently serialize the 9-tap loop, and matches the natural ConvTranspose data flow.
- Alternatively, fuse the min-over-channel reduction directly into the ConvTranspose epilogue: keep one program per (N, output-spatial tile), loop over all OC tiles internally accumulating a per-spatial running min, and never materialize the full (N, OC, OH, OW) tensor — this removes a 16×128×257×257 fp32 write/read (~4 GB) from the pipeline.
- Combined with the above, also fuse the sum-over-H into the same kernel by having each program own a (N, OW tile) and looping (h, oc) internally; the final output is only (N,1,1,OW)=16×257 elements, so the second kernel disappears entirely.
